To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SAF-A, the protein that binds SAR DNA with high affinity and specificity, is identical with hnRNA-binding protein hnRNP-U.
hnRNP- U/SAF-A is a multifunctional nuclear protein that binds DNA and RNA both in vivo and in in vitro experiments.
hnRNP U/SAF-A is a protein with multiple functions in the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterisation of proteins involved in nuclear organisation and the assembly of chromosomal subunits.

the identification of nuclear proteins involved in the organization and transcription of chromatin, and the characterization of their DNA-binding activities and the chromosomal sites of binding in vivo.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms involved in the organisation of eukaryotic chromatin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SAF-A protein binds both DNA and RNA and that the protein may have functions in chromosomal DNA organisation as well as in hnRNA processing.
the hnRNP-U/SAR protein, which is also known as hnRNP-SF, SAF-B and SAF-A, is a multifunctional protein with roles in hnRNA metabolism as well as in chromosomal DNA organisation.
hnRNP U/SAF-A is involved in the packaging of hnRNA and in the organisation of DNA in chromatin, and that the protein binds to both DNA and RNA with high specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hnRNP U is a nuclear matrix protein which binds DNA, and that hnRNP A1 is a nucleoplasmic protein which binds RNA.
SAF-A, the nuclear matrix protein which binds DNA with high affinity and specificity, also has RNA-binding properties and is identical with hnRNPU, the hnRNA-binding protein.

hnRNP U is a multifunctional nuclear protein which binds DNA, RNA and protein in vivo and in vivo and may thus be involved in the organisation of the chromosomal DNA, the processing and transport of hnRNA as well as the assembly and function of ribonucleoproteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hnRNP proteins can also bind DNA and may thus be involved in the organisation of the chromatin structure.
hnRNP U/SAF-A binds to DNA in vivo and in a sequence-specific manner in vitro.
hnRNP U is a multifunctional protein, with roles in hnRNA metabolism and in chromosomal organization.
